newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope in hospital, aide dismisses "medical fiction".
newsitem.headline: Pope in hospital, aide dismisses "medical fiction".

text.p: Pope John Paul went into hospital for an appendix operation in a blaze of media scrutiny on Sunday and his top cardinal dismissed reports that he was suffering from something more serious as "medical fiction".

The 76-year-old Pontiff was greeted at Rome's Gemelli hospital by Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro and senior staff including Professor Francesco Crucitti, the surgeon who will lead the team performing the operation.
"In all probability, the Holy Father will have his operation on Tuesday," a spokesman for Crucitti said, adding that no medical bulletin was expected to be issued until the surgery.

Dressed in white pontifical robes, the Pope waved to well wishers and an army of reporters after stepping from his black limousine to applause from patients, their families and medical staff leaning from balconies and watching from windows.

His recent frailty and fatigue have unleashed a flood of speculation that more than an inflammed appendix ails the leader of the world's 960 million Roman Catholics, a view dismissed on Sunday by one of the Vatican's most prominent prelates.
"It is all medical fiction," Cardinal Angelo Sodano said at the Gemelli, where the Pope will stay in a 10th floor suite with its own chapel and a view of the dome of St Peter's Basilica.
"He (the Pope) is very serene," said Sodano, who is Vatican Secretary of State. "He is a man of God and therefore he accepts everything from the hand of the one who is above."
The Pope earlier concluded a tiring beatification ceremony in St Peter's Square with a request for prayers.

"In asking you to accompany me with your prayer, I send cordial greetings to those in hospitals and clinics, knowing I can count on their spiritual solidarity," the Pope told tens of thousands of pilgrims.
"May the caring Virgin Mary watch over all of us," he said.
The stay will be the Polish-born Pontiff's sixth at the Gemelli since surgeons there saved his life after an assassination attempt in 1981.
Scores of journalists, photographers and television crews from around the world recorded the Pope's arrival, highlighting the intense interest in his health.

The Pope appeared tired during Sunday's almost three-hour beatification service and was troubled by an occasional cough. A marked trembling of his left hand, which some doctors say shows the Pope may have Parkinson's Disease, was also again evident.
The Pope, who has had major abdominal surgery three times since Turkish gunman Mehmet Ali Agca almost took his life in 1981, is expected to spend about a week at the Gemelli.

The surgery was announced by the Vatican on September 14 when it sought to end a flurry of speculation with a statement that said recurrent inflammation of the appendix was the cause of three bouts of fever the Pope has suffered since Christmas.
Some medical experts and Italian media have expressed scepticism about the statement and speculated that the Pope may be suffering from a new tumour, which the Vatican denies.
He had a colon tumour, which his doctors said was starting to turn malignant, removed in 1992 and complex abdominal surgery twice in 1981 after he was gravely wounded in the Agca shooting.
The Pontiff also had hip replacement surgery in 1994 after breaking his right leg in a bathroom fall and dislocated his right shoulder, which needed re-setting, in 1993.

Despite his ailments, the Pope has continued to travel, most recently to France last month on the 74th foreign visit of a global pilgrimage that has taken him the equivalent of 24 times around the world.
He has also maintained a full schedule of audiences and ceremonies at the Vatican, including Sunday's beatification ceremony put 16 more people on the road to sainthood.
